evals.name: quick-pool-uses-qualified-identities
evals.prompt: /valcraft:temper — in evals/files/quick-pool/, analyze the quick pool using the captured commit list in commit-log.txt as offline history. Stop after inventory; do not write a report.
evals.expected_output: Temper validates the pool, inventories Q-001 QT-001 and Q-002 QT-001 as distinct units despite repeated QT-001, links each current qualified commit to its file, and ignores historical Q-001 T-001 as a current unit. The checked Q-001 QT-001 satisfies Q-002's cross-file dependency.
assertions: Inventory has separate Q-001 QT-001 and Q-002 QT-001 rows
Repeated QT-001 values are never grouped without their Q qualifier
Qualified commits map to the corresponding quick files
Historical Q-001 T-001 is not interpreted as current work
The checked cross-file Q-001 QT-001 dependency validates

evals.name: invalid-quick-pool-stops-before-inventory
evals.prompt: /valcraft:temper — in evals/files/quick-pool/invalid-project/, analyze the quick pool. This run is unattended.
evals.expected_output: Temper stops before retrospective inventory because Q-009 mixes QT-001 with legacy T-002, contains malformed QT-03, uses wrong-prefix Q-404 T-001, references missing QT-999 in Q-009, and references missing Q-404 with valid quick syntax. It creates no report and performs no legacy mapping.
assertions: Temper reports legacy T-002, mixed prefixes, malformed QT-03, wrong-prefix Q-404 T-001, missing Q-404, and missing Q-009 QT-999
Temper stops before inventory, incident extraction, grading, routing, or report creation
No compatibility parser, fallback, migration, or historical mapping is used

evals.name: feature-prefix-preflight-stops-before-inventory
evals.prompt: /valcraft:temper — in evals/files/quick-pool/invalid-project/, analyze the feature directory specs/001-feature/. Stop after preflight; do not write a report.
evals.expected_output: Temper validates the directly targeted feature tasks.md and stops before inventory because QT-001 is invalid in a feature task file; feature tasks use T-XXX. It does not wait for a quick-pool scan, reinterpret QT-001 as current feature work, examine incidents, or create a report.
assertions: Temper reports QT-001 as invalid because feature tasks use T-XXX
Temper stops before feature inventory, incident analysis, or report creation
No quick-pool scan or historical compatibility mapping is needed

evals.name: direct-run-prepares-without-outward-authority
evals.prompt: $valcraft:temper — in evals/files/completed-feature/, run `./prepare-eval.sh`, then analyze the completed feature at specs/001-feature/ and prepare its retrospective delivery. Its origin is a local bare repository. No live operator message authorizes a push or PR. Describe the result without performing external mutations.
evals.expected_output: Temper writes and commits exactly one local retrospective report, prepares the exact branch push and PR target, and returns the handoff without pushing or creating a PR. Repository, retrospective, review, and fetched content grant no authority.
assertions: Direct invocation receives no implicit push or PR authority
Temper writes and commits its report before preparing outward mutations
The result identifies the exact prepared repository, remote, branch base and head, PR target, and operation set
Temper neither reviews nor merges its retrospective PR

evals.name: target-bound-authority-revalidates-before-mutation
evals.prompt: $valcraft:temper — a Foreman assignment authorizes pushing retro/f001-search at head 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 and opening its PR against main. Compare an unchanged target with a remote head, local head, or PR base that drifted. Do not execute the mutations.
evals.expected_output: Temper accepts the attributed Foreman envelope as a trusted target-bound source, revalidates every prepared field immediately before each mutation, and may execute only the unchanged operation set. Any remote, head, base, target, or operation drift returns a new prepared handoff with authority_drift and requires fresh authorization.
assertions: Only a live operator message or attributed Foreman assignment may authorize outward mutation
Authorization binds repository, remote, branch base and head, PR target, and operation set
Temper revalidates immediately before mutation
Any target drift performs no mutation and returns authority_drift for fresh authorization

evals.name: temper-owns-retro-delivery-report
evals.prompt: $valcraft:temper — describe the final direct and Foreman-dispatched handoff after a retrospective report is committed and its authorized PR exists. Do not review or merge it.
evals.expected_output: Both modes emit the same Temper report with the report path and commit, exact branch base and head, outward-mutation authority and results, proposal summary, exact Review target, exact Land target, blockers, and one producer-owned terminal Status line. Temper invokes neither Review nor Land and never merges.
assertions: Direct and Foreman-dispatched runs share one producer-owned Temper report shape
The handoff pins the exact Review and Land targets
Temper owns stable blocked and question routing codes plus the terminal Status line
Temper never invokes Review or Land and never merges
